findings.chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
findings.evidence: In-text references use the letter form: PDF p.111 "the quality claim itself is the §5.3(a)/§5.7 item still to validate on the target corpus"; PDF p.113 "Read them with the reconciliation note in §5.3(b) before comparing them with Ch 4's input-token per-dollar figures"; PDF p.122 "the §5.3(a) ~15% MAP uplift"; PDF p.118 "the parametric Q∗ in §5.3 shows how to decide". The chapter's own headings are numerically numbered with the letters only as decoration: "5.3.1. (a) Embedding-model selection for the retrieval leg", "5.3.2. (b) Generation-model selection for the answer leg", "5.3.3. (c) Base-model + RAG + guardrails vs fine-tuned model". The Preface fixes the rule: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4".
findings.issue: Chapter 5's cross-references point at subsections using "§5.3(a)/(b)/(c)", a numbering form that does not exist in the scheme the book declares and uses elsewhere (there is no subsection 5.3(a); the targets are 5.3.1–5.3.3). Under the book's own convention these references are unresolvable, and one of them ("the parametric Q∗ in §5.3") points to a whole section when the target is §5.3.3 — a third form of the same reference.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalise Ch. 5's internal references to §5.3.1 / §5.3.2 / §5.3.3 (and change "the parametric Q∗ in §5.3" to §5.3.3), or renumber the headings themselves to carry the letters as identifiers; then apply a global sweep for other "§N.M(x)" forms.
